Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with worsening right periorbital and generalized headache for 3 days, suggestive of probable migraine.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for 3 days, described as dull, sometimes sharper, mainly around the right eye but also generalized.
- Onset & progression: Gradually worsening over 3 days, started during work, more severe upon waking on the second day, persists with fluctuating intensity.
- Severity: Rated 8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light sensitivity), visual disturbances described as "shooting lights" at onset; difficulty focusing; no vomiting, no speech difficulty, no limb weakness.
- Pertinent negatives: No loss of vision, no recent head injury, no history of migraines, no fever, no rashes, no neck pain/stiffness, no prior similar severe headache episodes (past headaches typically resolve with Ibuprofen).
- Past medical history: "Otherwise fit and well," no chronic conditions mentioned.
- Family history: Mother and sister have migraines (mother's migraines are severe and triggered by season changes).
- Medications: No regular medications; wears glasses; took Ibuprofen (three tablets per day, dose unspecified) for this headache without relief.
- Allergies: None known.
- Social history: Lives with three housemates; works in IT (computers, increased screen time); socially smokes and drinks; no recent eye test; some recent work stress but not out of the ordinary; uses corrective lenses since age 5.

Examination:
- No examination findings recorded.
- No documented vitals.

Impression:
- Likely migraine headache, new onset (probable based on history and family history).

Plan:
- Discussed possible underdosing of Ibuprofen; advised up to two tablets three times daily if tolerated.
- Option to prescribe stronger analgesics, e.g., Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented), Paracetamol, or Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- To consider headache diary to monitor frequency and identify potential triggers.
- Follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.
- Advised to seek earlier review if headache worsens, neurological symptoms develop (vision changes, limb weakness), or if concerned.
- Discussion of prophylactic migraine treatment if recurrence noted at next review.
- Recommendation for routine eye test if symptoms suggest eye strain.

Quality checks:

●	Missing elements: No formal allergies and full meds reconciliation beyond what the patient reported; no documentation of physical exam or vital signs; no documented migraine diagnostic criteria beyond history; no review of systems beyond focused questions.
●	Internal conflicts: Patient answers "Yeah" then "No" when asked about neck pain/stiffness – conflict noted.
●	Transcript quality: Some conversational filler and minor ambiguities, but generally clear and complete for clinical documentation.
